Parallel metadata reports actual parallel use with three subagents, artifact_ok true, process_ok true, but official quality 0/165 and solution_passed false.
Current completed status evaluation supersedes aggregate fields and records a completed RepoZero Py2JS evaluation with solution_passed false and 0/165 samples.
Evaluation summary confirms expected 165 testcases, completed evaluator process, pass_rate 0.0, passed_samples 0, and solution_passed false.

timeline_reviews.summary: Top-level transport timeline covers the parent turn, file edits, validation probes, waits, child interruption, final response, and final task completion.

Parent probed source and executable behavior, spawned probe_cli and design_modules, wrote a CLI parser plus yaml_bridge shelling out to the executable, waited on children, interrupted probe_cli, and finalized.
probe_cli child independently explored CLI and YAML behavior, ran many executable probes, did not return a final result, and ended with a turn_aborted event after parent interruption.
design_modules child found the actual source/executable, probed basic behavior, and returned a recommendation not to use the executable in the final runtime because that would violate pure JS.

direct_file_reviews.summary: Task prompt is the same as parallel: produce pure Node.js ESM .mjs implementation in /output matching the Python YAML executable without npm dependencies or embedded Python.
Serial metadata reports no parallel use, no subagents, artifact_ok true, official quality 45/165, and solution_passed false.
Current completed status evaluation records completed RepoZero Py2JS evaluation with solution_passed false, passed_samples 45, total_samples 165, and no delegation.
Evaluation summary confirms expected 165 testcases, completed evaluator process, pass_rate 0.2727272727272727, passed_samples 45, and solution_passed false.
Final response lists local .mjs library files and says the implementation is pure Node.js ESM with manual process.argv parsing and reimplemented YAML load/dump behavior.

timeline_reviews.summary: Top-level serial transport timeline covers one single-agent turn with probing, file creation, verification commands, a parser fix, final response, and completion.

Serial parent probed executable behavior extensively, implemented local YAML parser/dumper modules, fixed a multiline sequence argv mismatch, ran parity scripts that printed ok, and finalized without child agents.

parallel.requirements: Recognized the same prompt requirements: pure Node.js ESM, .mjs files, manual --a parsing, no npm dependencies, no Python embedding, and output parity with PyYAML behavior.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Parent owned implementation while two children were spawned: probe_cli for additional executable behavior and design_modules for architecture advice. No child was assigned direct code ownership.
parallel.implementation: Parent wrote parser and program-name modules but implemented yaml_bridge.mjs around spawnSync('/workspace/dataset/test8_executable'), making the delivered YAML path a wrapper rather than a JS reimplementation.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Parent integrated its own wrapper files, did not incorporate the design child warning against executable runtime use, interrupted the probe child, and delivered test8.mjs plus library files.
parallel.verification: Parent compared its wrapper output against the executable on sampled CLI/YAML cases, which mainly verified the same executable-backed path rather than validating a pure JS YAML implementation.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: Final artifact violated the pure JS and no embedded Python/executable constraint, the probe child did not return a completed handoff, and official evaluation scored 0/165.

serial.requirements: Recognized pure ESM, .mjs suffixes, manual process.argv parsing, no npm dependencies, and the need to reimplement observed YAML load/dump behavior from the executable.
serial.plan_and_ownership: A single agent owned probing, design, implementation, integration, and verification end to end without delegation or handoff boundaries.
serial.implementation: Serial implemented cli_args.mjs plus yaml_types, yaml_utils, yaml_parse, yaml_dump, yaml.mjs, and test8.mjs as local ESM modules without shelling out to the executable.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Serial assembled the modules into /output/test8.mjs, patched its argument parser after detecting the multiline sequence issue, and delivered a coherent file set.
serial.verification: Serial ran repeated parity checks for samples, CLI error handling, multiline collections, quoted strings, numeric cases, explicit tags, comments, and normalized usage errors, with several scripts ending ok.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: Serial still failed the official threshold at 45/165, indicating its hand-written YAML subset was incomplete, but it satisfied more of the pure implementation contract than parallel.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel acknowledged the no-dependency and no-Python constraints but ultimately reported a runtime that delegates YAML transformation to the provided executable.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial treated the executable as an oracle and delivered a stated pure Node.js ESM reimplementation using local .mjs modules.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The central requirement difference is that serial attempted a native implementation while parallel broke the pure-JS/no-embedded-executable requirement.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel parent split work between its own implementation, a CLI-probing child, and a design-advice child, while keeping code ownership in the parent.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used no subagents and kept probing, implementation, parser fixes, and verification under one continuous owner.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel introduced handoff and monitoring obligations; serial avoided those boundaries but had less parallel exploration.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The design child returned the key interface constraint that the executable could be an oracle only, not part of the final runtime, but the parent proceeded against that handoff.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no cross-agent interface contract and encoded the interface locally through modules importing each other with .mjs suffixes.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel lost a critical returned coordination fact at the parent decision point; serial had no analogous handoff loss.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel implemented manual CLI parsing but put the YAML transformation behind node:child_process spawnSync of the bundled executable.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial implemented local YAML type, utility, parse, dump, wrapper, CLI, and entry modules as JavaScript files.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel achieved superficial parity by calling the oracle; serial built a limited but genuine JS YAML path.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel received the design child result, later waited on children, then interrupted the still-running probe_cli child before it returned a final handoff.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child lifecycle and used its own probe results immediately in subsequent patches and verification loops.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had one ignored completed result and one cancelled active child; serial had a direct local result lifecycle.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel parent alone wrote final files, so there was no observed concurrent write collision; the integration fault was semantic adoption of the wrong runtime strategy.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial parent alone wrote and patched the final module tree, including an argv fix after verification exposed the multiline sequence issue.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Neither run shows shared-write conflicts, but serial integrated its validation feedback while parallel integrated against returned design advice.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel verified examples against an executable-backed wrapper and then declared byte-for-byte parity despite violating the implementation constraint.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran broader side-by-side parity checks and normalized error handling checks after building a local implementation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel's verification was circular for YAML behavior; serial's verification tested its own JS parser/dumper and found/fixed a real argv mismatch.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel closed after two waits and an explicit interruption of probe_cli, with total runtime shorter but a zero-score artifact.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used more wall time but spent it on implementation, patches, and repeated checks before final delivery.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel saved time by closing around unfinished child work and an oracle wrapper; serial spent time completing a native implementation path.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The official relation is both_fail because both completed evaluations have solution_passed false. The material difference is still concrete: parallel delivered an executable-backed wrapper and scored 0/165, while serial delivered a pure local JS subset, verified it more thoroughly, and scored 45/165.
parallel_contributors: Ignored returned design advice warning that the executable should not be part of the runtime.
Interrupted an active probe child before a final handoff and closed with an incomplete local acceptance picture.
serial_contributors: Kept end-to-end ownership in one agent and implemented a local YAML parser/dumper module set.
Ran side-by-side parity checks and patched a multiline sequence argv mismatch before final delivery.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Serial's hand-written YAML subset remained incomplete, explaining why it still failed the overall official threshold.
Parallel's use of spawnSync around the task executable is also an implementation-contract violation, with the coordination evidence explaining why that wrong path survived review.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: Supported comparative quality-gap contributors; not an exclusive root cause and not a discordant pass/fail relation.

candidates.reason: Parallel had an implementation owner: the parent wrote the delivered parser, bridge, and entry files itself.
There were no separately owned component implementations requiring an unowned reconciliation step; the parent integrated its own files.
The parent owned and completed final artifact placement in /output, even though the chosen runtime design was wrong.
The parent controlled probing, implementation, validation, and delivery; the problem was child-result use, not an ownerless pipeline.
No mandatory serial preflight blocked productive work; the parent implemented while child probing and design activity overlapped.
Investigation did not complete as a separate first phase before implementation; the parent edited files while child work was still in progress.
The indispensable implementation path had an active parent owner; failure came from the wrong adopted strategy, not too little assigned capacity.
Only two children were spawned and the run did not time out; no collective fan-out consumed the finite budget before closure.
The incomplete child was a probe task, not a demonstrably overbroad implementation assignment whose size displaced required work.
The child task bodies are encrypted, and the observed child behavior shows awareness of pure-JS and oracle constraints rather than a proven missing initial requirement.
No independently produced components diverged at a file, export, input, or output interface; the children mainly produced probes and advice.
The key design warning did reach the parent; the issue was not that known information disappeared in transfer.
The design child handoff was concise and decision-structured, not too large to consume within the available decision window.
No receiver acted on superseded workspace or requirement state; the advice remained current when the parent implemented the opposite.
There were no incompatible returned child reports left unresolved; the actionable returned design advice was simply not used.
The final completion claim is downstream of the more specific unused child result about executable use, so retaining this would double-count the same consequence.
No replacement child or retry repeated prior work without inherited checkpoints; the run had one parent attempt and two initial child tasks.

candidates.reason: Parent explicitly interrupted the running probe_cli child after wait timeouts, and that child ended with turn_aborted instead of returning its final probe result.
candidates.realized_consequence: The active probe child's CLI/YAML findings were not finalized or returned before parent closure.
candidates.near_match_reason: The parent waited, but the directly evidenced lifecycle failure is the explicit child interruption and aborted child turn.

candidates.reason: No complete pure-JS candidate existed but was finalized too late; parallel's available candidate was executable-backed and not acceptable.
There is no child implementation change merged after integrated verification; parent validation followed its own file writes.
No child completed a delegated implementation for the parent to retrieve or merge; the child result was design advice, not code.
The probe child did not produce a completed concrete verifier finding that was trapped below the parent; it was interrupted before final return.
The child did not fail independently and then go untaken-over; the parent itself interrupted it, making Early Child Termination the direct label.
The design child returned a concrete warning not to include the executable in the final runtime, but the parent created and delivered a runtime bridge around that executable.
candidates.realized_consequence: The returned design constraint was not adopted, and the final artifact used the prohibited executable-backed runtime path that scored 0/165.
candidates.near_match_reason: The final unsupported completion claim is real but downstream; the more specific observable coordination boundary is the unused completed child result.

candidates.reason: The parent waited twice near closure, but it also listed agents and then explicitly interrupted the active probe child, so the lifecycle boundary is more specific.
Children did not write competing implementation paths; the parent produced the final file tree itself.
No two live agents are observed editing the same source/config file or reconciling each other's concurrent same-file changes.
No agent replaced a non-entry source file produced or actively owned by another live agent.
The entrypoint was written by the parent only; there is no deliverable replacement while another agent owned or used it.
No broad cleanup, rebuild, or promotion overwrote multiple outputs from another agent in the final workspace.
Although the workspace was shared, only the parent wrote implementation files, so no unstable provenance or shared-write problem materialized.
No generated artifact, cache, temporary path, tool, or auxiliary implementation from one concurrent actor was consumed by another as stable input.
